ledger.note: 1357 (bridging): the Yuan side fights the Ispah army for Putian and the approach to Fuzhou. The page dates only the seizure of Quanzhou (March 1357) and the end (1366); Toghon Temür and Chen Youding commanded the Yuan side.

region.text: Quanzhou, seized by the Ispah army in March 1357

ledger.note: March 1357: the Ispah army, led by Sayf ad-Din and Amir ad-Din, seizes Quanzhou. The army was organised by the Persian Shi'a Muslims of Quanzhou to defend their group; the commanders took control of the city and suppressed the formerly dominant Sunnis.

1362: the Ispah army collapses into internal conflict and Yawuna, a Quanzhou Arab Sunni official, becomes its leader. The leadership passes from the Persian Shi'a commanders to a Sunni; the holding is unchanged.

notes: Written for ea-06-x from the Ispah rebellion, Chen Youding and Red Turban Rebellions pages. Cliopatria has no row. The Ispah page is an article about a rebellion (infobox Dates 1357-1366, Result Yuan victory, Capital: not stated in the source), not a state; it is written as a rebel state because the Ispah army held Quanzhou for nine years and the scope names the rebellions that broke the Yuan apart. Not on any page opened: the extent of the land held, the dates of Putian and Fuzhou, the date of the Quanzhou massacre; the Chen Youding page gives 1367 for the Ming takeover of Fujian where the Ispah page gives 1366 for the end of the rebellion. Chen Youding's Yuan-loyal Fujian (1366-1367) is a Yuan warlord regime of one year and is left to the Yuan and Ming dossiers. Counterparts needing dossiers: yuan-dynasty (ea-06-a).
